content.content:
---
name: dart-native
description: "Expert knowledge for building apps with DartNative — the framework that renders Flutter-API Dart code as real native views (UIKit on iOS, the View system on Android). Use when: writing DartNative screens and widgets, checking what is and isn't Flutter-compatible, looking up widget APIs and their native lowerings, or migrating Flutter code. For porting an existing Flutter app (project setup, build failures, white screens), also load the dart-native-porting skill."
---

# DartNative — Developer Guide

DartNative lets you write Dart with the Flutter widget API and renders it as
**real native views**: `Text` → `UILabel`/platform text, `ListView` →
`UITableView`/`RecyclerView`, `TextField` → `UITextField`, `AppBar` → a real
navigation bar (Liquid Glass on iOS 26), `BottomNavigationBar` → the native
tab bar. There is no rendering engine and no bridge: Dart drives the views
directly, and layout runs on Yoga (flexbox) with Flutter's sizing rules.

**The compatibility contract, honestly stated:** DartNative is *almost*
Flutter-compatible. Most widgets are identical or near-identical; some are
deliberately different where real native structure demands or enables it;
a few Flutter patterns are absent by design. The per-widget truth is
`docs/widgets.md` in this repo — consult it before assuming an API.

## Toolchain

```sh
dn create my_app     # scaffold a project
cd my_app
dn pub get           # fetches the prebuilt dartnative packages (dartpub.dev)
dn run               # build + launch on a connected device/simulator
```

`dn` is DartNative's CLI (get it at dartpub.dev). All familiar subcommands
work (`run`, `build`, `pub get`, hot reload during `run`). Building and
testing is free; a dartpub.dev subscription is needed to ship to production.

## App startup

```dart
import 'package:dartnative/dartnative.dart';
import 'dartnative_plugin_registrant.dart'; // generated by dn pub get

void main() {
  // MUST be the first line: registers the platform bindings and every
  // dartnative_* plugin's FFI symbols. Missing it = white screen, no crash.
  DartNativePluginRegistrant.registerAll();
  runApp(const MyScreen());
}
```

- Pass the root **screen** to `runApp` directly. Do **not** wrap it in
  `App(home: ...)` — `App` only provides theme/navigator inheritance and
  does not mount `home` natively (white screen). Use `App` only for a
  named-`routes:` map.
- Multi-screen apps register routes once: `registerRoutes({'/detail': (_) =>
  const DetailScreen()})`, then `Navigator.pushNamed(context, '/detail')`.
- The one import is `package:dartnative/dartnative.dart`. Never import
  `package:flutter/...` or `dart:ui` — DartNative ships its own painting
  and geometry types, and `dart:ui` is not part of the runtime. Read the
  device locale with `Platform.localeName` from `dart:io`.

**Why explicit registrations exist at all** — in Flutter the engine does
this invisibly: plugins self-register through GeneratedPluginRegistrant +
method channels, fonts are bundled by the build, and Skia IS the renderer.
DartNative has no engine layer: every capability is Dart talking to native
code over FFI, and FFI symbols must be LOADED before first use. So each
capability is one explicit, cheap registration in main() — and forgetting
one produces a characteristic symptom, never a crash:

| Forgotten | Symptom |
|---|---|
| `DartNativePluginRegistrant.registerAll()` | white screen (no bindings — nothing can render); a missing plugin symbol → that plugin's calls fail |
| `registerSkiaFactories()` | `CanvasSurface`/Skia painting renders nothing |
| `SystemChrome.defaultStyle` | screens inherit device-default chrome (e.g. wrong status-bar icon color on the first frame) |

The full startup anatomy (the playground's main.dart is the canonical
reference):

```dart
void main() {
  DartNativePluginRegistrant.registerAll(); // ALWAYS, first: bindings +
                        // every dartnative_* plugin's FFI symbols. The file
                        // is generated from your pubspec on every dn pub
                        // get — add a plugin, done. No per-plugin setup.
  SystemChrome.defaultStyle = const SystemUiOverlayStyle(...); // app-wide
                        // chrome default; screens override in initState and
                        // the navigator restores this on pop
  registerSkiaFactories();                  // ONLY with dartnative_skia:
                        // enables CanvasSurface / Skia-backed painting
  runApp(const HomeScreen());
}
```

Plugin-specific initializers (e.g. `Firebase.initializeApp()`,
`Sqlite.ensureInitialized()`) also live here, after `registerAll()`.

Custom fonts need no line here: declare them under `flutter: fonts:` in
pubspec.yaml, as in Flutter, and use them by family name
(`TextStyle(fontFamily: ...)`, `IconData(..., fontFamily: ...)`). The app
loads them itself, on iOS when it starts and on Android when a family is
first used.

## The catalog, by porting relevance

Statuses from `docs/widgets.md` (the authoritative per-widget reference —
consult it for any param-level question).

### Ports unchanged — use as in Flutter

- **Layout**: `Row`, `Column`, `Flex`, `Expanded`, `Flexible`, `Spacer`,
  `Stack`/`Positioned`, `Padding`, `Container`, `SizedBox`,
  `ConstrainedBox`, `DecoratedBox`, `Align`/`Center`, `SafeArea`,
  `AspectRatio`, `Wrap`, `FractionallySizedBox`,
  `IntrinsicWidth`/`IntrinsicHeight`, `FittedBox`, `ColoredBox`,
  `IndexedStack`, `LayoutBuilder`, `Divider`, `Opacity`, `Visibility`,
  `IgnorePointer`/`AbsorbPointer`, `RepaintBoundary`, `ClipRect`,
  `ClipRRect`, `ClipOval`. `Align` takes any alignment and `widthFactor` /
  `heightFactor`. `double.infinity` fills as in Flutter
  (`SizedBox(width: double.infinity)`, `SizedBox.expand()`,
  `SizedBox.fromSize(size: Size.infinite)`, `BoxConstraints.expand()`,
  `Image(width: double.infinity)`), and a `SizedBox.expand()` child makes
  its `Stack` fill.
- **Text**: `Text`, `RichText`/`TextSpan`, `TextStyle`, `TextPainter`. A
  pubspec font family with a file per weight and style draws each one's own
  file, `w100` to `w900` and italic, as in Flutter; a missing bold is drawn
  thickened and a missing italic slanted.
- **Scrolling**: `ListView`, `SingleChildScrollView`, `GridView`,
  `CustomScrollView` with `SliverList`(+`.builder`), `SliverGrid`,
  `SliverToBoxAdapter`, `SliverPadding`, `SliverFillRemaining`,
  `SliverAppBar`; `NestedScrollView` with a `SliverAppBar` header that
  collapses natively; `TabBar` / `TabBarView` with `TabController` or
  `DefaultTabController`, as in Flutter. **`ListView.builder`,
  `ListView.separated` and `GridView.builder` are lazy, as in Flutter**:
  items are built as they near the screen and let go once they are more
  than `cacheExtent` off it (250 points unless set), on the platform's own
  list and grid, the ones `FastList` and `FastGrid` use, so a long,
  data-driven list keeps its Flutter code and scrolls smoothly at any
  `itemCount`. An item's `State` does not outlive it off screen: keep what
  must survive in the model. `GridView.extent`, or a
  `SliverGridDelegateWithMaxCrossAxisExtent`, takes as many columns as fit
  the grid's width. A `ListView` or `GridView` of `children`, and one that
  shrink-wraps or never scrolls, builds every item, as Flutter lays those
  out whole. A grid cell's content fills the cell, as in Flutter. Reach for
  `FastList` / `FastGrid` for what only they offer; see below.
- **Images**: `Image.network` (cached), `Image.asset`, `CircleAvatar`.
- **Animation — the full suite**: `AnimationController` (+ both ticker
  mixins), `CurvedAnimation`, `AnimatedBuilder`/`AnimatedWidget`,
  `FadeTransition`, `SlideTransition`, `ScaleTransition`, `SizeTransition`,
  `RotationTransition`, `AlignTransition`, `DecoratedBoxTransition`,
  `FractionalTranslation`, `AnimatedOpacity`, `AnimatedContainer`,
  `AnimatedSwitcher`, `Transform`. Nested transforms combine, also through
  `AnimatedScale`, `AnimatedSlide`, `Opacity` or a widget of yours between
  them. One diff: `controller.duration` is final — set it in the
  constructor, or pass `duration:` to `animateTo()` / `animateBack()`.
- **Theming**: `ThemeData.light()/.dark()`, `ColorScheme`, `TextTheme`
  (15 slots) — via `App(theme: ...)`. Explicit styles remain the common
  DartNative idiom, but ported `Theme`-based code has a target.
- **Input & focus**: `TextField` (see diffs), `FocusNode`, `Focus`,
  `FocusScope`, `TextEditingController`.
- **Controls**: `Switch`, `Slider`, `CircularProgressIndicator`,
  `LinearProgressIndicator`, `SegmentedControl`, buttons (`Button` with
  variants, `FloatingActionButton`, `BarButtonItem`), `Badge`, native
  menus.
- **State & misc**: `setState`, `ValueNotifier` + `ValueListenableBuilder`,
  `ScrollController` (vertical or horizontal: `offset`, `jumpTo` and
  `animateTo` work along the scroll axis), `GestureDetector` (tap callbacks
  in Flutter's order: `onTapDown`, then `onTapUp` and `onTap`, or
  `onTapCancel`; incl. `HitTestBehavior.translucent` — fully supported
  sibling-forwarding), `async` callbacks (the code after an `await` in
  `onTap` runs as in Flutter), `Dismissible` (swipe a row away),
  `RepaintBoundary` + `RenderRepaintBoundary.toImage` (capture a widget as
  an image; `ui.` types from `package:dartnative/canvas.dart`),
  `WidgetsBinding.instance.addPostFrameCallback`,
  `WidgetsBindingObserver` (`didChangeAppLifecycleState`,
  `didChangeMetrics`, `didHaveMemoryPressure`, registered with
  `WidgetsBinding.instance.addObserver`),
  `MediaQuery.of(context)` (`size`, `padding`, `viewInsets.bottom` live
  keyboard height, `devicePixelRatio`, `platformBrightness`,
  `textScaleFactor`), `SystemChrome` (orientations, overlay style,
  `defaultStyle`, status/navigation bar colors), `dartnative_intl` for
  l10n.
- **Background work**: `compute` (it runs on `runInBackground`, which
  costs the UI thread less than `Isolate.run`). Where Flutter code calls
  `Isolate.run(() => work(x))`, write `runInBackground(() => work(x))`:
  same rules, less work on the UI thread.

Layout parity is engineered: layouts land where Flutter puts them. That
includes a `Row`'s rule: a text in a Row stays on one line and runs past
the row's end, unless it sits in an `Expanded` or `Flexible`, so write the
`Expanded` you would write in Flutter. `Flexible` keeps Flutter's loose fit.
A text that wraps takes the whole width it is given, as in Flutter: give a
chat bubble's text `textWidthBasis: TextWidthBasis.longestLine` so the
bubble ends at its longest line.

### Different on purpose — adopt the DartNative form

**`Scaffold`** — full surface: `appBar`, `body`, `backgroundColor`,
`bottomNavigationBar`, `bottomInputBar` (keyboard-attached bar — chat
inputs go HERE, never in `bottomNavigationBar`), `bottomAccessory` (strip
above the bottom bar; iOS 26 lowers it to the native tab accessory),
`floatingActionButton`,
`extendBody`, `extendBodyBehindAppBar`, `resizeToAvoidBottomInset`
(default true; the body is **lifted, not resized**: when the focused
field is in the body, the body moves up by exactly the amount the field
is obscured, on the keyboard's own animation, and the `AppBar` stays put;
`false` keeps the body still), and
`brightness` — **declare it `Brightness.dark` on any dark-by-colors
screen** or system materials (keyboard, glass, scroll-edge fades) render
light on light-mode devices.

**`AppBar`** — full surface: `leading`, `title`, `actions` (arbitrary
widgets; `BarButtonItem` gives the default-padded action),
`automaticallyImplyLeading`, `showBackTitle`, `backgroundColor`,
`toolbarHeight`, `actionsPadding`, `subtitle`, `largeTitle` +
`largeTitleSize` (medium/large — native large-title collapse on iOS 26,
the M3 collapsing top app bar on Android), `searchBar` (the bar region
becomes the search pill: App Store in-place search on iOS 26, the real M3
search app bar on Android; `title` is skipped when set),
`titleGlassBackground` (default false), `actionsGlassBackground` (default
true — set false for self-decorated action widgets like avatars),
`brightness` (forces the bar's glass tone; iOS 26 only).

**`TextField`** — a real platform field. `InputDecoration` is
intentionally minimal (hint, `border: InputBorder.none`, content padding);
borders/fills come from a wrapping `Container`. Multiline growth via
`minLines`/`maxLines` works.

**`BottomNavigationBar`** — surface: `items`, `currentIndex`, `onTap`,
`iconColor`/`selectedIconColor`, label styles, `indicatorColor`,
`backgroundColor` (ignored on iOS 26 — the glass pill IS the background),
`scrollBehavior` (minimize/hide on scroll — lowers to a real
`UITabBarController` on iOS 26), `onSearchQueryChanged`; items support
`subtitle`, `enabled`, `activeIcon`, and `BottomNavigationBarItem.search()`
(the iOS 26 separated search pill).

**Navigation** — `Navigator.push(context, PageRoute(builder: (_) =>
Screen()))` (push always takes a Route) / `Navigator.pushNamed` (+
`registerRoutes`) / `pop`. `PageRoute(builder:, transition:, duration:,
settings: '/route-name')` with `RouteTransition.slideFromRight` (default) /
`.slideFromBottom` (modal) / `.slideFromLeft` / `.slideFromTop` / `.fade`.
No `PageRouteBuilder`/`transitionsBuilder` — drop custom transition
curves.

**Dialogs / overlays** — `showAlert(context:, title:, message:,
actions:)` → `Future<int>` (tapped index); `showActionSheet`;
`showModalSheet(context:, builder:)` (native detent sheet, Dart content);
`showModalBottomSheet` / `showDialog` (light-dismiss
cards); `showDatePicker`; `showColorPicker` (the system picker on iOS;
completes with `null` on Android); `showMediaPicker` (from the
`dartnative_media_picker` plugin); `BottomSheet`. A sheet, alert, action
sheet, date picker or colour picker opened from inside a sheet appears on
top of it.
`ScaffoldMessenger.showSnackBar` works (routes to the native toast).

**`CustomPaint`** — supported, painting through Core Graphics /
`android.graphics.Canvas`. `CanvasSurface` (optional `dartnative_skia`)
only for SkSL shaders (`RuntimeEffect`) and other GPU work.

**DartNative additions worth adopting during a port**: `FastList` /
`FastGrid` / `MasonryFastGrid` (native cell recycling; `itemCount` +
`itemBuilder`; built content held only for a window around the screen,
250 points by default, sized with `cacheExtent` in points or
`keepAliveCount` in items; `recycleItems` to reuse the rows the window lets
go; `onScroll`; `FastListController.scrollToItem`; `onReorder`) for long
feeds that need those options; `PageView` /
`PageController` on the platform's own paging, or `FastList(pagingEnabled:
true)` for a full-screen feed that also windows with `keepAliveCount`
(`viewportFraction` other than 1 is not supported: a peeking carousel is a
horizontal `FastList`); `GlassEffectContainer`
(`borderRadius`, `tint`, `interactive`, `brightness`) for real iOS 26
glass; `DynamicColor.colorScheme(brightness:)` for Material You;
`VideoPlayer` via `dartnative_video_player`.

### Not available — plan around these

| Missing | Porting move |
|---|---|
| `SelectableText` | `Text(selectable: true)` — long-press to select and copy |
| `Offstage` ⚠️ | The offstage child is UNMOUNTED (state lost) — Flutter keeps it mounted. Use `IndexedStack` for state-preserving show/hide |
| `Theme.of` inheritance beyond `App(theme:)` | Pass styles explicitly where the theme object isn't enough |
| `InheritedWidget`/`Provider`/Riverpod | `signal<T>` + `.watch(context)`; `Provided<T>` for per-subtree values |
| `RenderObject`/`RenderBox` layer | Doesn't exist — Yoga computes frames natively |
| `MethodChannel` + plugins using one | FFI only: such plugins crash at launch (`Setting a message handler before the FlutterEngine has been run`). Swap for dartnative_* or FFI/pure-Dart equivalents |
| `WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized()` | `DartNativePluginRegistrant.registerAll()` |
| `rootBundle.load` | `loadAssetBytes('assets/foo.json')` — sync, returns `Uint8List?` |

## State management

`setState` works as in Flutter. For shared state, the built-in signals:

```dart
class AppStore {
  final counter = signal<int>(0);          // observable field
  void increment() => counter.value++;
}
final store = AppStore();

// In build(): subscribes this element; rebuilds on change.
Text('${store.counter.watch(context)}');
```

Migration mapping: `context.watch<T>()` / `ref.watch(p)` →
`store.field.watch(context)`; `context.read<T>()` / `ref.read(p.notifier)` → the store
reference; `StateProvider` → `signal<T>`; `ProviderScope(overrides:)` →
`Provided<T>(value:, child:)`. Delete `ProviderScope`/`MultiProvider`
wrappers and `Consumer*` base classes. `ValueListenableBuilder` works
unchanged (or call `controller.watch(context)` inline).

## Platform powers (use them — they're the point)

- **Declare dark screens**: `Scaffold(brightness: Brightness.dark)` on
  dark-by-colors screens — system materials (keyboard, glass, scroll-edge
  effects) render in the declared trait; without it a light-mode device
  paints them light.
- **iOS 26 Liquid Glass**: a translucent `AppBar.backgroundColor` (alpha <
  1) opts into the real frosted bar; no color = the clear bar with the
  system scroll-edge ramp; `GlassEffectContainer` for glass anywhere.
  Everything no-ops cleanly pre-26 and on Android. For a fallback of your
  own where there is no glass, branch on `isIOS26`, not on the OS version:
  `isIOS26 ? GlassEffectContainer(...) : Container(decoration: ...)`.
- **Search in the bar**: `AppBar.searchBar: SearchBar(...)` — the App Store
  in-place choreography on iOS 26, the real Material 3 search app bar on
  Android. `title` is skipped when set.
- **Large titles**: `AppBar.largeTitle` collapses natively on scroll (the
  system large title on iOS 26; the M3 collapsing top app bar on Android).
- **Chat input**: `Scaffold.bottomInputBar` — the bar rides the exact system
  keyboard curve, including interactive dismiss.

## Conventions that scale

Taken from the starter app; adopt them in any app you generate.

- **Every pushed route carries a registered name.** Add each screen to
  `registerRoutes`, then push it by name (`Navigator.pushNamed`) or by
  builder with the same name in `PageRoute(settings: '/name')`. On hot
  restart the stack is rebuilt from those names; a route without a
  registered name is dropped from the stack.
- **Notifier for tree shape, signal for a value inside one element.** A
  `ChangeNotifier` per concern (`AppRepository.notes..watch(context)`)
  rebuilds every watcher when the list of things changes; a `Signal` on a
  field (a note's text) repaints only the widget watching it. Do not add a
  state-management package; extend this pattern.
- **Themed screens declare their trait.** A themed `Scaffold` passes
  `brightness: palette.brightness` so native surfaces (keyboard, alerts,
  glass) follow the app theme, and reads colours from the palette rather
  than hardcoding them.
- **Drawer items are sections, not routes.** A drawer selects what the home
  screen renders in place; push a route only for secondary screens such as
  settings, or back would walk through destinations.
- **Screens never touch storage or the network directly.** They talk to
  state notifiers and services, which talk to SQLite and the API.
- **Per-install configuration** (keys, endpoints) comes from a bundled
  `.dnkeys` file read through `DnKeys.get` (`dartnative_keys`); features that
  need the network degrade to local behaviour when a key is absent.
- **Always the `dn` CLI**, never `flutter`: `dn pub get`, `dn run`,
  `dn build`.

## Common mistakes

1. `App(home: screen)` as root → white screen. Pass the screen to `runApp`.
2. Missing `DartNativePluginRegistrant.registerAll()` first in `main()` →
   white screen, no crash.
3. `bottomNavigationBar` used for a chat input → the keyboard covers it,
   as it covers a native tab bar. Keyboard-attached bars go in
   `bottomInputBar`.
4. A custom top bar inside `body` → the keyboard pushes it off-screen. Top
   bars belong in `Scaffold.appBar` (it's a real `UINavigationBar`, pinned
   by the OS). If you must, set `resizeToAvoidBottomInset: false`.
5. `setState` in `initState` → not mounted yet; schedule it.
6. Importing `package:flutter/...` or unaliased `dart:ui` → type conflicts.
   One import: `package:dartnative/dartnative.dart`.

## Localization

ARB files and a generated `S` class, as in Flutter, generated by
`dartnative_intl`. Five things differ; each one is a real failure mode.

```yaml
dev_dependencies:
  dartnative_intl: ^1.0.1

flutter_intl:
  enabled: true
  arb_dir: l10n
  output_dir: lib/generated
  class_name: S
  main_locale: en
```

direction is read once at startup from the OS. Choosing Arabic inside your app
translates its text but does not mirror layout; that needs a per-app language
change on Android or a device language change on iOS.

# DartNative — Developer Guide

DartNative lets you write Dart with the Flutter widget API and renders it as
**real native views**: `Text` → `UILabel`/platform text, `ListView` →
`UITableView`/`RecyclerView`, `TextField` → `UITextField`, `AppBar` → a real
navigation bar (Liquid Glass on iOS 26), `BottomNavigationBar` → the native
tab bar. There is no rendering engine and no bridge: Dart drives the views
directly, and layout runs on Yoga (flexbox) with Flutter's sizing rules.

**The compatibility contract, honestly stated:** DartNative is *almost*
Flutter-compatible. Most widgets are identical or near-identical; some are
deliberately different where real native structure demands or enables it;
a few Flutter patterns are absent by design. The per-widget truth is
`docs/widgets.md` in this repo — consult it before assuming an API.

## Toolchain

```sh
dn create my_app     # scaffold a project
cd my_app
dn pub get           # fetches the prebuilt dartnative packages (dartpub.dev)
dn run               # build + launch on a connected device/simulator
```

`dn` is DartNative's CLI (get it at dartpub.dev). All familiar subcommands
work (`run`, `build`, `pub get`, hot reload during `run`). Building and
testing is free; a dartpub.dev subscription is needed to ship to production.

## App startup

```dart
import 'package:dartnative/dartnative.dart';
import 'dartnative_plugin_registrant.dart'; // generated by dn pub get

void main() {
  // MUST be the first line: registers the platform bindings and every
  // dartnative_* plugin's FFI symbols. Missing it = white screen, no crash.
  DartNativePluginRegistrant.registerAll();
  runApp(const MyScreen());
}
```

- Pass the root **screen** to `runApp` directly. Do **not** wrap it in
  `App(home: ...)` — `App` only provides theme/navigator inheritance and
  does not mount `home` natively (white screen). Use `App` only for a
  named-`routes:` map.
- Multi-screen apps register routes once: `registerRoutes({'/detail': (_) =>
  const DetailScreen()})`, then `Navigator.pushNamed(context, '/detail')`.
- The one import is `package:dartnative/dartnative.dart`. Never import
  `package:flutter/...` or `dart:ui` — DartNative ships its own painting
  and geometry types, and `dart:ui` is not part of the runtime. Read the
  device locale with `Platform.localeName` from `dart:io`.

**Why explicit registrations exist at all** — in Flutter the engine does
this invisibly: plugins self-register through GeneratedPluginRegistrant +
method channels, fonts are bundled by the build, and Skia IS the renderer.
DartNative has no engine layer: every capability is Dart talking to native
code over FFI, and FFI symbols must be LOADED before first use. So each
capability is one explicit, cheap registration in main() — and forgetting
one produces a characteristic symptom, never a crash:

| Forgotten | Symptom |
|---|---|
| `DartNativePluginRegistrant.registerAll()` | white screen (no bindings — nothing can render); a missing plugin symbol → that plugin's calls fail |
| `registerSkiaFactories()` | `CanvasSurface`/Skia painting renders nothing |
| `SystemChrome.defaultStyle` | screens inherit device-default chrome (e.g. wrong status-bar icon color on the first frame) |

The full startup anatomy (the playground's main.dart is the canonical
reference):

```dart
void main() {
  DartNativePluginRegistrant.registerAll(); // ALWAYS, first: bindings +
                        // every dartnative_* plugin's FFI symbols. The file
                        // is generated from your pubspec on every dn pub
                        // get — add a plugin, done. No per-plugin setup.
  SystemChrome.defaultStyle = const SystemUiOverlayStyle(...); // app-wide
                        // chrome default; screens override in initState and
                        // the navigator restores this on pop
  registerSkiaFactories();                  // ONLY with dartnative_skia:
                        // enables CanvasSurface / Skia-backed painting
  runApp(const HomeScreen());
}
```

Plugin-specific initializers (e.g. `Firebase.initializeApp()`,
`Sqlite.ensureInitialized()`) also live here, after `registerAll()`.

Custom fonts need no line here: declare them under `flutter: fonts:` in
pubspec.yaml, as in Flutter, and use them by family name
(`TextStyle(fontFamily: ...)`, `IconData(..., fontFamily: ...)`). The app
loads them itself, on iOS when it starts and on Android when a family is
first used.

## State management

`setState` works as in Flutter. For shared state, the built-in signals:

```dart
class AppStore {
  final counter = signal<int>(0);          // observable field
  void increment() => counter.value++;
}
final store = AppStore();

// In build(): subscribes this element; rebuilds on change.
Text('${store.counter.watch(context)}');
```

Migration mapping: `context.watch<T>()` / `ref.watch(p)` →
`store.field.watch(context)`; `context.read<T>()` / `ref.read(p.notifier)` → the store
reference; `StateProvider` → `signal<T>`; `ProviderScope(overrides:)` →
`Provided<T>(value:, child:)`. Delete `ProviderScope`/`MultiProvider`
wrappers and `Consumer*` base classes. `ValueListenableBuilder` works
unchanged (or call `controller.watch(context)` inline).

## Platform powers (use them — they're the point)

- **Declare dark screens**: `Scaffold(brightness: Brightness.dark)` on
  dark-by-colors screens — system materials (keyboard, glass, scroll-edge
  effects) render in the declared trait; without it a light-mode device
  paints them light.
- **iOS 26 Liquid Glass**: a translucent `AppBar.backgroundColor` (alpha <
  1) opts into the real frosted bar; no color = the clear bar with the
  system scroll-edge ramp; `GlassEffectContainer` for glass anywhere.
  Everything no-ops cleanly pre-26 and on Android. For a fallback of your
  own where there is no glass, branch on `isIOS26`, not on the OS version:
  `isIOS26 ? GlassEffectContainer(...) : Container(decoration: ...)`.
- **Search in the bar**: `AppBar.searchBar: SearchBar(...)` — the App Store
  in-place choreography on iOS 26, the real Material 3 search app bar on
  Android. `title` is skipped when set.
- **Large titles**: `AppBar.largeTitle` collapses natively on scroll (the
  system large title on iOS 26; the M3 collapsing top app bar on Android).
- **Chat input**: `Scaffold.bottomInputBar` — the bar rides the exact system
  keyboard curve, including interactive dismiss.

## Conventions that scale

Taken from the starter app; adopt them in any app you generate.

- **Every pushed route carries a registered name.** Add each screen to
  `registerRoutes`, then push it by name (`Navigator.pushNamed`) or by
  builder with the same name in `PageRoute(settings: '/name')`. On hot
  restart the stack is rebuilt from those names; a route without a
  registered name is dropped from the stack.
- **Notifier for tree shape, signal for a value inside one element.** A
  `ChangeNotifier` per concern (`AppRepository.notes..watch(context)`)
  rebuilds every watcher when the list of things changes; a `Signal` on a
  field (a note's text) repaints only the widget watching it. Do not add a
  state-management package; extend this pattern.
- **Themed screens declare their trait.** A themed `Scaffold` passes
  `brightness: palette.brightness` so native surfaces (keyboard, alerts,
  glass) follow the app theme, and reads colours from the palette rather
  than hardcoding them.
- **Drawer items are sections, not routes.** A drawer selects what the home
  screen renders in place; push a route only for secondary screens such as
  settings, or back would walk through destinations.
- **Screens never touch storage or the network directly.** They talk to
  state notifiers and services, which talk to SQLite and the API.
- **Per-install configuration** (keys, endpoints) comes from a bundled
  `.dnkeys` file read through `DnKeys.get` (`dartnative_keys`); features that
  need the network degrade to local behaviour when a key is absent.
- **Always the `dn` CLI**, never `flutter`: `dn pub get`, `dn run`,
  `dn build`.

## Common mistakes

1. `App(home: screen)` as root → white screen. Pass the screen to `runApp`.
2. Missing `DartNativePluginRegistrant.registerAll()` first in `main()` →
   white screen, no crash.
3. `bottomNavigationBar` used for a chat input → the keyboard covers it,
   as it covers a native tab bar. Keyboard-attached bars go in
   `bottomInputBar`.
4. A custom top bar inside `body` → the keyboard pushes it off-screen. Top
   bars belong in `Scaffold.appBar` (it's a real `UINavigationBar`, pinned
   by the OS). If you must, set `resizeToAvoidBottomInset: false`.
5. `setState` in `initState` → not mounted yet; schedule it.
6. Importing `package:flutter/...` or unaliased `dart:ui` → type conflicts.
   One import: `package:dartnative/dartnative.dart`.

# Widget Reference

DartNative ships a widget set designed to be source-compatible with Flutter, under one import: `package:dartnative/dartnative.dart`.

This reference covers what is available, what isn't, and what to use instead when a Flutter widget has no native equivalent.

As in Flutter, a colour or text style set back to `null` returns the widget to its default look, so `color: selected ? accent : null` works.

---

## Layout

| Widget | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Column` | ✅ | `textDirection` sets which side `CrossAxisAlignment.start` and `end` mean for this column only; by default the nearest `Directionality`. As in Flutter, a column keeps within the height its parent offers, and children that overflow start at its top, whatever `mainAxisAlignment`, and draw past its end. Inside a column that does not stretch its children, a `Center`, an aligned `Container` or a `Stack`, a column is as wide as its widest child, as in Flutter; a child that takes the whole width, such as a `Row` or a text field, or `CrossAxisAlignment.stretch`, makes it as wide as the space it is given. A column directly in a `Scaffold` body still takes the whole width |
| `Row` | ✅ | `textDirection` sets the order of this row only, for example a phone number kept left to right in a right-to-left screen; by default the nearest `Directionality`. As in Flutter, a child that is not in an `Expanded` or `Flexible` has no width limit: a text wider than the row stays on one line and runs past the row's end. Put it in an `Expanded` or `Flexible` to wrap it or end it with an ellipsis. A row keeps within the width its parent offers, and children that overflow start at its start, whatever `mainAxisAlignment`, and draw past its end. With `CrossAxisAlignment.stretch` every child is as tall as the row, even one with a height of its own, as in Flutter; inside an `IntrinsicHeight` the row is as tall as its tallest child. A child wrapped in a `Padding` keeps its own height. A row inside another row, outside an `Expanded`, is as wide as its content, as in Flutter |
| `Flex` | ✅ | `textDirection` as on `Row` and `Column` |
| `Expanded` | ✅ | Takes its share of the free space whatever its content, as in Flutter: two `Expanded` children with `flex: 1` are the same width |
| `Flexible` | ✅ | As in Flutter, the child gets at most its share of the free space and a smaller child keeps its own size (`fit: FlexFit.loose`, the default); `FlexFit.tight` fills the share like `Expanded` |
| `Spacer` | ✅ | |
| `Stack` | ✅ | As in Flutter, a `Positioned` child that reaches past the `Stack` makes it clip: everything past its edges is cut. A child that is not positioned never makes it clip. `clipBehavior: Clip.none` lets every child draw outside, as a badge at `top: -8` needs. A child with a key keeps its state when the children are reordered, added or removed, as in Flutter. A `Stack` whose children are all positioned takes the biggest size its parent allows, as in Flutter |
| `Positioned` | ✅ | A child of the `Stack` or what a child's `build` returns, also inside a `Visibility`, as in Flutter. Its child is as wide as `left` and `right` leave it, or as `width` says; with only one of them it is as wide as its content. The same holds for `top`, `bottom` and `height`, as in Flutter. `Positioned.directional(textDirection:, start:, end:, …)` places by start and end in the direction you give; `Positioned.fromRect` and `Positioned.fromRelativeRect` (with `RelativeRect`) as in Flutter |
| `PositionedDirectional` | ✅ | A `Positioned` by `start` and `end` instead of left and right, as in Flutter: they follow the nearest `Directionality`, or the app's direction, so a badge at `end: 8` sits on the right in left-to-right text and on the left in right-to-left text, and moves when the direction changes |
| `Padding` | ✅ | |
| `Container` | ✅ | `width: double.infinity`, `height: double.infinity` and `constraints: BoxConstraints.expand()` take the whole of that side of the space the parent gives, as `SizedBox` does. `transform` and `transformAlignment` transform the whole box, as in Flutter. A `Container` with only a child is no box of its own, as in Flutter: a child that a transform moves out of it still takes taps where it is drawn. `clipBehavior` as in Flutter: by default nothing is clipped, so a rounded or circular decoration shapes the fill, border and shadow and a child that reaches the corners keeps its own; `Clip.antiAlias` (or `hardEdge`) cuts the child to the decoration's shape, and the shadow still shows |
| `SizedBox` | ✅ | `double.infinity` takes the whole of that side of the space the parent gives, as in Flutter: `SizedBox(width: double.infinity)` spans a column, and `SizedBox.expand()` or `SizedBox.fromSize(size: Size.infinite)` fill both sides. As a child of a `Stack` that is not `Positioned`, it makes the `Stack` fill that side of its space too. In a `Wrap`, `width: double.infinity` makes the box as wide as the `Wrap`, on a line of its own. In a `Row` or `Column`, along its direction, where Flutter reports an error, the box takes the space the other children leave; in a scroll view, along the scrolling direction, it keeps its child's size. As in Flutter, a parent that sets its children's width, such as a `Column` that stretches its children, a vertical `ListView` or a box with a width, gives that width to a `SizedBox`, `Container` or `Image` whatever width of its own it has, and a `Row` that stretches its children or a horizontal `ListView` gives its height the same way. Inside an `IntrinsicWidth`, a column that stretches its children is as wide as its widest child, and every child as wide as the column, as in Flutter |
| `ConstrainedBox` | ✅ | Lays its child out within the limits, as in Flutter, and is laid out as `Container(constraints:)`. A size the parent sets, such as a grid cell, an `Expanded`, or the width of a stretched column or a list, takes precedence over the limits, as in Flutter. A minimum height reaches the child, which fills the box. |
| `DecoratedBox` | ✅ | Paints its decoration behind its child, or over it with `position: DecorationPosition.foreground`, where touches still reach the child. It takes its child's size: no padding, not even for a border, and nothing is clipped, so the child keeps its own corners. It paints what a `Container`'s decoration paints: a colour or a linear gradient (a radial gradient shows its first colour), the top-left corner radius on all four corners, a circle (a capsule on a box that is not square), a border drawn on every side as its top side is, and the first shadow |
| `Align` / `Center` | ✅ | Any alignment from -1 to 1 on each axis: `Alignment(0.5, 0)` puts the child three quarters of the way to the right, and an animated alignment moves smoothly. `widthFactor` and `heightFactor` size the box as a multiple of its child, unless the room it is given is fixed (an `Expanded` share, a sized parent), which it then fills. Along a `Row`'s or a `Column`'s main axis an `Align` is as long as its child, as in Flutter: a `Column` holding a `Center` puts the centred text at the top, not in the middle of the screen. A factor on an axis where the child fills all the room it is given (a `ListView`, `SizedBox.expand()`) leaves the box filling that axis |
| `SafeArea` | ✅ | |
| `Divider` / `VerticalDivider` | ✅ | On iPhone the table separator: one pixel in the separator grey. |
| `AspectRatio` | ✅ | |
| `Opacity` | ✅ | A child at opacity 0 still takes taps, as in Flutter |
| `Visibility` | ✅ | Default flags match Flutter (hidden child is replaced and its state disposed). The full `maintain*` set is supported: with `maintainState: true` the child stays mounted and is hidden natively — pair with `maintainSize` to keep its layout slot. A hidden child takes no taps, unless `maintainInteractivity` is set |
| `Offstage` | ⚠️ | The offstage child is unmounted (state lost) — Flutter keeps it mounted at zero size. For state-preserving show/hide, use `IndexedStack` |
| `ClipRRect` | ✅ | Rounded rect clip via `Container(decoration: BoxDecoration(borderRadius: ...))` |
| `ClipRSuperellipse` | ✅ | iOS squircle clip — wraps child in `ShapeDecoration(shape: RoundedSuperellipseBorder(...))` |
| `ClipOval` | ✅ | Circle clip via `BoxDecoration(shape: BoxShape.circle)` |
| `ClipRect` | ✅ | As large as its child, or as the room it is given when that is fixed (an `Expanded` share, a sized parent), and clips what reaches past its edges. `clipBehavior: Clip.none` draws the child unclipped |
| `Wrap` | ✅ | flex-wrap. `alignment`, `runAlignment`, `spacing`, `runSpacing` and `crossAxisAlignment` work as in Flutter: runs that overflow start at the wrap's start, a child is at most the wrap's width, and what overflows a wrap in a box of fixed size draws past it |
| `FractionallySizedBox` | ✅ | Sizes its child to a fraction of the space around it, placed by `alignment`. Where that space is not fixed (a `Column` that does not stretch, a `Center`), the box itself is the fraction |
| `IntrinsicWidth` / `IntrinsicHeight` | ✅ | Sizes the child to its own width or height: a `Column` of buttons as wide as the widest, a `Row` as tall as its tallest child |
| `FittedBox` | ✅ | Lays the child out at its natural size, then scales it into the box per `fit` (every `BoxFit`) and places it by `alignment`; `clipBehavior` cuts what reaches past the box |
| `ColoredBox` | ✅ | Prefer over `Container(color:…)` for simple fills |
| `IgnorePointer` | ✅ | Blocks hit testing for the subtree. Decided when a pointer goes down: a drag already in progress keeps flowing when `ignoring` flips mid-gesture |
| `AbsorbPointer` | ✅ | Touches in its box reach neither its child nor what is behind it; widgets around it, such as an outer `GestureDetector` or a scroll view, still get them. Decided when a pointer goes down |
| `IndexedStack` | ✅ | One child visible at a time; all children stay mounted (state + scroll position preserved — the tab-switcher pattern). Sizing note: fills its parent (Flutter sizes to the largest child) — wrap in a `SizedBox` when you need an intrinsic size |
| `LayoutBuilder` | ✅ | Provides parent `BoxConstraints` to the builder |
| `Directionality` | ✅ | `Directionality.of(context)` works everywhere: every screen starts from the direction the platform lays the app out in, which is right-to-left only when the app declares a right-to-left language (`CFBundleLocalizations` on iOS, `android:supportsRtl` on Android). Wrap a subtree to override it: its rows, cross-axis alignment, directional padding and alignment and `TextAlign.start` follow it. Horizontal scroll views keep the app's direction. `MediaQueryData.textDirection` carries the same value |
| `EdgeInsetsDirectional` / `AlignmentDirectional` | ✅ | `EdgeInsetsDirectional.fromSTEB` included; `start` and `end` follow the nearest `Directionality`; `AlignmentDirectional` is its own type, as in Flutter, and `AlignmentGeometry.resolve` gives the physical `Alignment` |
| `TextAlign.start` / `TextAlign.end` | ✅ | Follow `Text.textDirection` when given, else the nearest `Directionality`. `Row`, `Column` and `Wrap` mirror on their own under right-to-left |
| Right-to-left chrome | ✅ | The `AppBar` mirrors with the rest of the app: the back arrow, the title, a search field and the actions swap sides, the back chevron points the way back, and `actionsPadding`'s start and end follow the reading direction. The bar's own items are placed by the framework, so this holds on both hosts and on both platforms |
| `Card` | ✅ | Without a `color`, the platform's card: Material's outlined card on Android (the surface colour with a thin edge, no shadow), white with a shadow on iOS. `elevation` left out is that default; a `color` of your own drops the edge. `clipBehavior` as in Flutter: nothing is clipped by default; use `Clip.antiAlias` when the content reaches the corners, such as an image at the top. |
| `ListTile` | ✅ | Leading / title / subtitle / trailing row. On Android the title and subtitle wear Material's list item type and colours unless you style them. On Android the tile is at least 56 dp tall, 72 with a subtitle, with its content centred and 8 dp above and below the text, as in Flutter. On iPhone the subtitle is 15 pt in the secondary style, the text colour at half opacity, and the row is the 70 pt row of a plain list, 15 pt above and below the two lines. `onTap` and `onLongPress` make the row answer a press as the platform's own list rows do: the grey highlight of a table row on iPhone, the ripple of a Material list item on Android. `enabled: false` ignores them and dims the row, as in Flutter. |
| `Table` | ✅ | Column-sized grid layout |
| `BackdropFilter` | ✅ | Native backdrop blur (Gaussian) — `UIVisualEffectView` (iOS) / `RenderEffect` (Android) |
| `ImageFiltered` | ✅ | Blurs the child's own content (Gaussian) |
| `ShaderMask` | ✅ | Shows the child through a `LinearGradient` or `RadialGradient` (`createShader(bounds)`): `BlendMode.dstIn` keeps it where the gradient is opaque, `BlendMode.dstOut` where it is transparent, and the default `BlendMode.modulate` with white colours works as `dstIn`. The system draws the mask, so a child that moves inside it, such as a scrolling title, is not redrawn. The child shows only inside the mask's box |
| `SnackBar` | ✅ | Shown via `ScaffoldMessenger.of(context).showSnackBar`; `content`, `backgroundColor`, `duration`, and `action: SnackBarAction(label:, onPressed:)` |
| `RepaintBoundary` | ✅ | Captures a widget as an image, as in Flutter: give it a `GlobalKey`, then `(key.currentContext!.findRenderObject() as RenderRepaintBoundary).toImage(pixelRatio: 3)`, and `image.toByteData(format: ui.ImageByteFormat.png)` for a PNG, or `image.toJpeg(quality: 90)` for a JPEG at a quality from 0 to 100 (DartNative's own: Flutter has no JPEG there; transparent pixels come out white). Both files are encoded by the platform's own encoder, off the UI thread; on iPhone the PNG favours speed over size, so use the JPEG for a small file. `ui.Image` and `ui.ImageByteFormat` come from `import 'package:dartnative/canvas.dart' as ui;`, where Flutter code imports `dart:ui`. The image is the widget as the platform draws it, all of it, also the parts scrolled out of sight. A video, a map or a camera preview inside it is left out, as Flutter leaves out a platform view, and on Android so is a `BackdropFilter` blur. It adds no view and does not change the layout |

---

## Measuring Widgets

| API | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `context.mounted` | ✅ | False once the widget has left the tree and its `State` has been disposed. Check it after an `await` before using the context again, the same as in Flutter |
| `GlobalKey.currentContext` | ✅ | Resolves to the mounted element for that key |
| `findRenderObject()` | ✅ | Returns the `RenderBox` of the first native view the widget draws into, as in Flutter, so it works on the context of a `StatelessWidget` or a `StatefulWidget` as well as on a `Container` or a `Text`. Null before the widget is on screen |
| `context.size` | ✅ | The size of that view, as in Flutter |
| `RenderBox.size` | ✅ | The native view's size, in logical pixels |
| `RenderBox.localToGlobal` | ✅ | Converts to screen coordinates. Use it whenever the answer has to be the truth rather than a calculation — a bar that follows the keyboard does not sit where inset arithmetic says. With `ancestor:`, in the coordinates of a box the view is inside, as in Flutter |
| `RenderBox.globalToLocal` | ✅ | Converts screen coordinates to the view's, as in Flutter, `ancestor:` included |
| `findAncestorStateOfType` | ✅ | The `State` of the nearest ancestor of that type, as in Flutter; `findRootAncestorStateOfType` returns the furthest. The ancestor lookups stop at the root of the screen the widget is on: a pushed screen, a sheet and a dialog each have a tree of their own. For the `Navigator`, use `Navigator.of(context)`, and for a `Scaffold`'s drawer, `Scaffold.of(context)` |
| `findAncestorWidgetOfExactType` | ✅ | The nearest ancestor widget of exactly that type, as in Flutter |
| `findAncestorRenderObjectOfType` | ✅ | The nearest ancestor's render object of that type, as in Flutter: a `RepaintBoundary`'s, or the `RenderBox` of a view the widget is inside |
| `visitAncestorElements` | ✅ | Visits each ancestor, from the parent up, until the visitor returns `false`, as in Flutter |

---

## Text & Input

| Widget | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Text` | ✅ | `UILabel`. A `Text` with no colour takes the platform's default text colour: the label colour on iOS; on Android the colour a `TextView` with no style has, the theme's secondary text colour. A `ListTile` title and the bar title use the primary text colour, as Material's styles do. Under a screen with a forced `Scaffold.brightness`, or in a sheet or dialog opened over it, it is the primary colour of that brightness. `textWidthBasis` works as in Flutter: a text that wraps takes the whole width it is given; `TextWidthBasis.longestLine` makes it as wide as its longest line, for a chat bubble. |

The ancestor lookups stop at the root of the screen the widget is on: a pushed screen, a sheet and a dialog each have a tree of their own. For the `Navigator`, use `Navigator.of(context)`, and for a `Scaffold`'s drawer, `Scaffold.of(context)` |
76	| `findAncestorWidgetOfExactType` | ✅ | The nearest ancestor widget of exactly that type, as in Flutter |
77	| `findAncestorRenderObjectOfType` | ✅ | The nearest ancestor's render object of that type, as in Flutter: a `RepaintBoundary`'s, or the `RenderBox` of a view the widget is inside |
78	| `visitAncestorElements` | ✅ | Visits each ancestor, from the parent up, until the visitor returns `false`, as in Flutter |

82	## Text & Input
83	
84	| Widget | Status | Notes |
85	|---|---|---|
86	| `Text` | ✅ | `UILabel`. A `Text` with no colour takes the platform's default text colour: the label colour on iOS; on Android the colour a `TextView` with no style has, the theme's secondary text colour. A `ListTile` title and the bar title use the primary text colour, as Material's styles do. Under a screen with a forced `Scaffold.brightness`, or in a sheet or dialog opened over it, it is the primary colour of that brightness. `textWidthBasis` works as in Flutter: a text that wraps takes the whole width it is given; `TextWidthBasis.longestLine` makes it as wide as its longest line, for a chat bubble. |
87	| `RichText` / `TextSpan` | ✅ | `NSMutableAttributedString` — per-span font, color, weight, italic, underline, strikethrough. `const TextSpan(...)` works as in Flutter. `TextSpan.recognizer: TapGestureRecognizer` supported for tappable spans. `textWidthBasis` as on `Text`. `TextSpan` is not `const` — remove `const` from all `TextSpan(...)` calls |

If `InputDecoration.contentPadding` is omitted, the field uses the platform's own inset: 14 all round on iOS, and on Android the plain field's 4dp beside and 10dp above and below the text, or Material's 16dp for a Material field (override explicitly to customize). `inputFormatters` run on every edit before the keystroke is drawn, caret included: `FilteringTextInputFormatter` (`digitsOnly`, `allow`, `deny`), `LengthLimitingTextInputFormatter`, or your own `TextInputFormatter` over `TextEditingValue` / `TextSelection` `onSubmitted` fires when the user taps the keyboard's action key — the key itself is chosen by `textInputAction` (Done, Go, Search, Send, Next) — and receives the field's current text. As in Flutter, only single-line fields report a submission: in a multiline field that key inserts a newline. The key then ends the edit as in Flutter: Done (the default for a one-line field when you set no `textInputAction`; Apple's search field on iPhone keeps its Search key), Go, Search and Send close the keyboard and take the focus away, and Next moves to the following text field, on iPhone too. On the last field Next closes the keyboard, as a native form does; in Flutter, Next goes to the next widget that can take the focus, a button included, and from the last one back to the first. If your `onSubmitted` moves the focus itself, your choice wins. **The field owns its box:** `InputDecoration.border` given as an `OutlineInputBorder` (its side's colour and width, one radius), `focusedBorder`, `enabledBorder` and `disabledBorder` by Flutter's precedence, and `filled` with a `fillColor`, are drawn by the native field itself, so a decorated field is one native view: the keyboard reveals the whole box, and the focused outline follows focus. `InputBorder.none`, an `UnderlineInputBorder` and no border leave the platform's own look. A box an app draws around a field is not the field, and the keyboard keeps only the field visible, as a native Android field does. On Android, a decoration with `labelText`, `helperText`, an `OutlineInputBorder` or `filled` is drawn by Material's own text field: the label floats onto the edge when the field takes focus, the helper line sits below, and the outlined or filled box has Material's colours and its 56dp height; an explicit border side, corner radius or `fillColor` still applies, and `hintText` is the placeholder. A field with none of those is Android's plain field with its underline; `InputBorder.none` removes it. On iOS the field stays bare and `labelText`/`helperText` are not drawn. `errorBorder` is not drawn. On iPhone a field whose `OutlineInputBorder` keeps its default side is the platform's own rounded field, 34 pt with its grey bezel; `labelText` stands in for a missing `hintText` there; a bare field is the text line alone, with no inset. **Search fields:** a single-line field whose `prefixIcon` is the search icon (`Icons.search` or `CupertinoIcons.search`) is the platform's own search field. On iPhone it is Apple's search field, as tall as the one in a search bar, with its clear button while the user types; Apple draws its box and places its text there, so the decoration's border, fill and `contentPadding` do not apply. On Android a field with a label, a border or a fill shows the icon in Material's own place at the start of the box; set `prefixIconPadding` to place it yourself. `prefixIconSize` defaults to the platform's size. `clearButtonMode` adds a clear button (on Android Material's own round ✕ at the end of the box, which hides a `suffixIcon` while it shows), and `clearIconColor` tints it. |
89	| `TextEditingController` | ✅ | `text`, `value`, `selection`, `clear()`. Typing updates the controller before `onChanged`; a selection the user makes, or a caret they move, updates `selection` and tells the listeners, without calling `onChanged`. Setting `selection` or `value` moves the caret, setting `text` keeps it where the field has it. Focusing the field from code keeps a selection the controller already has, as in Flutter |
90	
91	> **Font size units.** dartnative renders text using real native APIs, so `TextStyle.fontSize` follows each platform's conventional unit — **UIKit points** on iOS (fixed, does not scale with Dynamic Type) and **SP** on Android (scales with the user's font-size accessibility setting). This is identical to what you get writing native UIKit or Android code directly.
92	| `TextPainter` | ✅ | Drop-in replacement backed by the platform's text measurement — call `layout(maxWidth:)` then read `.size`. As in Flutter, a text that wraps is as wide as the `maxWidth` given (`textWidthBasis: TextWidthBasis.longestLine` keeps the longest line), and `minWidth` is honoured |
93	| `RenderParagraph` | ✅ | Drop-in replacement — `layout(BoxConstraints)` + `.size`; no RenderObject tree required |
94	| `SelectableText` | ✅ | Covered by `Text(selectable: true)` — long-press to select/copy on BOTH platforms. Plain `Text` stays `UILabel` / `TextView`; the flag swaps in a read-only `UITextView` (iOS) / read-only `EditText` (Android), so use plain `Text` when selection isn't needed. Its width is Flutter's `SelectableText`'s: a text that wraps takes the whole width it is given, or its longest line with `textWidthBasis: TextWidthBasis.longestLine`, and the box keeps a 3-point margin for the caret. A dedicated `SelectableText` class is not exported; pass the flag. |
95	| `ValueListenableBuilder<T>` | ✅ | Full `StatefulWidget` — subscribes via `addListener`, passes typed `value` to builder, cleans up on `dispose`. Drop-in from Flutter. |
96	| `StreamBuilder<T>` | ✅ | Full `StatefulWidget` — manages `StreamSubscription`, full `ConnectionState` lifecycle (none → waiting → active → done). Drop-in from Flutter. |
97	| `FutureBuilder<T>` | ✅ | Full `StatefulWidget` — a completion after the builder left the tree, or after its future was replaced, is ignored. Drop-in from Flutter. |

106	
107	| Widget | Status | Notes |
108	|---|---|---|
109	| `ListView` | ✅ | A list of `children` lays out all its items, as in Flutter. 111	| `KeepAlive` / `AutomaticKeepAliveClientMixin` | ✅ | Keep an item of a lazy list built while it is off screen, its `State` included: `ListView.builder`, `.separated`, `GridView.builder`, a lazy `CustomScrollView`, `FastList` and `FastGrid`. `AutomaticKeepAlive` is accepted and shows its child |
112	| `ListView.separated` | ✅ | A `separatorBuilder` between each two items; lazy like `builder` |

116	| `SliverList` / `SliverList.builder` | ✅ | |
117	| `SliverFixedExtentList` | ✅ | `.builder` and `.list`; every item takes `itemExtent` |
118	| `SliverGrid` | ✅ | `.count` and `.extent` constructors; `.extent` takes as many columns as fit its width; cells come in rows |
119	| `SliverToBoxAdapter` | ✅ | |
120	| `SliverPadding` | ✅ | Pads the sliver as a whole, as in Flutter |
121	| `SliverFillRemaining` | ✅ | Takes what the viewport has left after the slivers before it, as in Flutter. Inside a `SliverPadding` the padding before it counts, as in Flutter. In a reversed view too, its child sits right against the slivers before it |
122	| `SliverAppBar` | ✅ | Every named parameter of Flutter's widget is accepted. 123	| `GridView` | ✅ | `.count`, `.extent` and `.builder`. `GridView.builder` is lazy, as in Flutter: cells are built as they near the screen and let go once they are more than `cacheExtent` off it (250 points unless set), on the platform's own grid, the one `FastGrid` uses, so it scrolls smoothly at any `itemCount`; a cell's `State` ends off screen unless the cell asks to stay, as in `ListView.builder`. With no `padding` it keeps clear of the status bar and the home indicator as `ListView` does. With `shrinkWrap: true` or `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` every cell is built, as in Flutter. `GridView.extent`, or a `SliverGridDelegateWithMaxCrossAxisExtent`, takes as many columns as fit cells no wider than `maxCrossAxisExtent`, so a wider screen or a rotation gets more columns. 124	| `ScrollController` | ✅ | On `ListView`, `GridView`, `SingleChildScrollView` and `CustomScrollView`: `offset`, `position.pixels` and `position.maxScrollExtent` follow the scroll along the view's axis, and `position.maxScrollExtent` and `position.viewportDimension` are known once the view is laid out, before any scroll, as in Flutter. `jumpTo` and `animateTo` move the view along it, so a horizontal `ListView`, `GridView` or `SingleChildScrollView` reads and moves sideways. A notification goes up the screen it was sent on: pushed screens, sheets and dialogs each have their own. `OverscrollNotification`, and scroll notifications from `PageView`, `NestedScrollView` and `TabBarView`, are not sent yet, and a list inside one of those three still reports a `depth` of 0 above it |
126	| `PageView` | ✅ | `PageView`, `.builder`, `.custom` and `PageController`; each swipe settles on one page on the platform's own paging. `PageController.page` is the page the view rests on before the first swipe. 127	| `NestedScrollView` | ✅ | Flutter's API: `headerSliverBuilder`, `body`, `floatHeaderSlivers`, `NestedScrollViewState` through a `GlobalKey`, `sliverOverlapAbsorberHandleFor`, `SliverOverlapAbsorber` and `SliverOverlapInjector`. # Widget Reference

DartNative ships a widget set designed to be source-compatible with Flutter, under one import: `package:dartnative/dartnative.dart`.

This reference covers what is available, what isn't, and what to use instead when a Flutter widget has no native equivalent.

As in Flutter, a colour or text style set back to `null` returns the widget to its default look, so `color: selected ? accent : null` works.

---

## Layout

| Widget | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `Column` | ✅ | `textDirection` sets which side `CrossAxisAlignment.start` and `end` mean for this column only; by default the nearest `Directionality`. As in Flutter, a column keeps within the height its parent offers, and children that overflow start at its top, whatever `mainAxisAlignment`, and draw past its end. Inside a column that does not stretch its children, a `Center`, an aligned `Container` or a `Stack`, a column is as wide as its widest child, as in Flutter; a child that takes the whole width, such as a `Row` or a text field, or `CrossAxisAlignment.stretch`, makes it as wide as the space it is given. A column directly in a `Scaffold` body still takes the whole width |
| `Row` | ✅ | `textDirection` sets the order of this row only, for example a phone number kept left to right in a right-to-left screen; by default the nearest `Directionality`. As in Flutter, a child that is not in an `Expanded` or `Flexible` has no width limit: a text wider than the row stays on one line and runs past the row's end. Put it in an `Expanded` or `Flexible` to wrap it or end it with an ellipsis. A row keeps within the width its parent offers, and children that overflow start at its start, whatever `mainAxisAlignment`, and draw past its end. With `CrossAxisAlignment.stretch` every child is as tall as the row, even one with a height of its own, as in Flutter; inside an `IntrinsicHeight` the row is as tall as its tallest child. A child wrapped in a `Padding` keeps its own height. A row inside another row, outside an `Expanded`, is as wide as its content, as in Flutter |
| `Flex` | ✅ | `textDirection` as on `Row` and `Column` |
| `Expanded` | ✅ | Takes its share of the free space whatever its content, as in Flutter: two `Expanded` children with `flex: 1` are the same width |
| `Flexible` | ✅ | As in Flutter, the child gets at most its share of the free space and a smaller child keeps its own size (`fit: FlexFit.loose`, the default); `FlexFit.tight` fills the share like `Expanded` |
| `Spacer` | ✅ | |
| `Stack` | ✅ | As in Flutter, a `Positioned` child that reaches past the `Stack` makes it clip: everything past its edges is cut. A child that is not positioned never makes it clip. `clipBehavior: Clip.none` lets every child draw outside, as a badge at `top: -8` needs. A child with a key keeps its state when the children are reordered, added or removed, as in Flutter. A `Stack` whose children are all positioned takes the biggest size its parent allows, as in Flutter |
| `Positioned` | ✅ | A child of the `Stack` or what a child's `build` returns, also inside a `Visibility`, as in Flutter. Its child is as wide as `left` and `right` leave it, or as `width` says; with only one of them it is as wide as its content. The same holds for `top`, `bottom` and `height`, as in Flutter. `Positioned.directional(textDirection:, start:, end:, …)` places by start and end in the direction you give; `Positioned.fromRect` and `Positioned.fromRelativeRect` (with `RelativeRect`) as in Flutter |
| `PositionedDirectional` | ✅ | A `Positioned` by `start` and `end` instead of left and right, as in Flutter: they follow the nearest `Directionality`, or the app's direction, so a badge at `end: 8` sits on the right in left-to-right text and on the left in right-to-left text, and moves when the direction changes |
| `Padding` | ✅ | |
| `Container` | ✅ | `width: double.infinity`, `height: double.infinity` and `constraints: BoxConstraints.expand()` take the whole of that side of the space the parent gives, as `SizedBox` does. `transform` and `transformAlignment` transform the whole box, as in Flutter. A `Container` with only a child is no box of its own, as in Flutter: a child that a transform moves out of it still takes taps where it is drawn. `clipBehavior` as in Flutter: by default nothing is clipped, so a rounded or circular decoration shapes the fill, border and shadow and a child that reaches the corners keeps its own; `Clip.antiAlias` (or `hardEdge`) cuts the child to the decoration's shape, and the shadow still shows |
| `SizedBox` | ✅ | `double.infinity` takes the whole of that side of the space the parent gives, as in Flutter: `SizedBox(width: double.infinity)` spans a column, and `SizedBox.expand()` or `SizedBox.fromSize(size: Size.infinite)` fill both sides. As a child of a `Stack` that is not `Positioned`, it makes the `Stack` fill that side of its space too. In a `Wrap`, `width: double.infinity` makes the box as wide as the `Wrap`, on a line of its own. In a `Row` or `Column`, along its direction, where Flutter reports an error, the box takes the space the other children leave; in a scroll view, along the scrolling direction, it keeps its child's size. As in Flutter, a parent that sets its children's width, such as a `Column` that stretches its children, a vertical `ListView` or a box with a width, gives that width to a `SizedBox`, `Container` or `Image` whatever width of its own it has, and a `Row` that stretches its children or a horizontal `ListView` gives its height the same way. Inside an `IntrinsicWidth`, a column that stretches its children is as wide as its widest child, and every child as wide as the column, as in Flutter |
| `ConstrainedBox` | ✅ | Lays its child out within the limits, as in Flutter, and is laid out as `Container(constraints:)`. A size the parent sets, such as a grid cell, an `Expanded`, or the width of a stretched column or a list, takes precedence over the limits, as in Flutter. A minimum height reaches the child, which fills the box. |
| `DecoratedBox` | ✅ | Paints its decoration behind its child, or over it with `position: DecorationPosition.foreground`, where touches still reach the child. It takes its child's size: no padding, not even for a border, and nothing is clipped, so the child keeps its own corners. It paints what a `Container`'s decoration paints: a colour or a linear gradient (a radial gradient shows its first colour), the top-left corner radius on all four corners, a circle (a capsule on a box that is not square), a border drawn on every side as its top side is, and the first shadow |
| `Align` / `Center` | ✅ | Any alignment from -1 to 1 on each axis: `Alignment(0.5, 0)` puts the child three quarters of the way to the right, and an animated alignment moves smoothly. `widthFactor` and `heightFactor` size the box as a multiple of its child, unless the room it is given is fixed (an `Expanded` share, a sized parent), which it then fills. Along a `Row`'s or a `Column`'s main axis an `Align` is as long as its child, as in Flutter: a `Column` holding a `Center` puts the centred text at the top, not in the middle of the screen. A factor on an axis where the child fills all the room it is given (a `ListView`, `SizedBox.expand()`) leaves the box filling that axis |
| `SafeArea` | ✅ | |
| `Divider` / `VerticalDivider` | ✅ | On iPhone the table separator: one pixel in the separator grey. |
| `AspectRatio` | ✅ | |
| `Opacity` | ✅ | A child at opacity 0 still takes taps, as in Flutter |
| `Visibility` | ✅ | Default flags match Flutter (hidden child is replaced and its state disposed). The full `maintain*` set is supported: with `maintainState: true` the child stays mounted and is hidden natively — pair with `maintainSize` to keep its layout slot. A hidden child takes no taps, unless `maintainInteractivity` is set |
| `Offstage` | ⚠️ | The offstage child is unmounted (state lost) — Flutter keeps it mounted at zero size. For state-preserving show/hide, use `IndexedStack` |
| `ClipRRect` | ✅ | Rounded rect clip via `Container(decoration: BoxDecoration(borderRadius: ...))` |
| `ClipRSuperellipse` | ✅ | iOS squircle clip — wraps child in `ShapeDecoration(shape: RoundedSuperellipseBorder(...))` |
| `ClipOval` | ✅ | Circle clip via `BoxDecoration(shape: BoxShape.circle)` |

| API | Status | Notes |

| `findRenderObject()` | ✅ | Returns the `RenderBox` of the first native view the widget draws into, as in Flutter, so it works on the context of a `StatelessWidget` or a `StatefulWidget` as well as on a `Container` or a `Text`. Null before the widget is on screen |

### High-performance native lists

content.content:
130	### High-performance native lists
131	
132	These are DartNative-specific widgets built directly on the platform's own list machinery — the scroll physics, momentum and rubber-banding are UIKit's / `RecyclerView`'s, not a re-implementation. That buys three things that are hard to get elsewhere:
133	
134	- **Native scrolling feel** — the platform draws only on-screen cells (cell-container recycling), so scrolling stays smooth at any list length, even with heavy cells.
135	- **Exact index jumps** — `jumpToItem(5000)` lands precisely on item 5000 via the platform's own index APIs (`scrollToRow` / `scrollToPosition`), instantly, no pixel-offset guessing. This is notoriously hard to achieve with offset-based scroll controllers.
136	- **Rows are built as they near the viewport** — the mount builds the rows that fill the first screen, the margin beyond them right after the first frame, and each further row is built as the scroll approaches it, so `itemCount` is a number, not a cost: a list of ten thousand rows launches like one of thirty. Give `itemExtent` when every row has the same height and the list's geometry is exact from the start; otherwise an unbuilt row takes the average of the rows measured so far, as Flutter's estimated extents do.
137	- **Bounded memory (content windowing)** — the list or grid keeps built content only for the visible rows and a window around them: 250 points on each side by default, as Flutter's `cacheExtent`, or `keepAliveCount` rows (cells, in a grid) on each side: **built content is O(visible + the window), independent of `itemCount`**. Rows leaving the window release everything they built (images, animations, native views) while keeping their exact height — scroll position never moves; rows re-entering rebuild *before* they reach the screen, so there's no visible seam. Give rows an `Image.placeholder` (e.g. `Shimmer`) to cover deep scroll-back reloads.
138	
139	| Widget | Status | iOS | Android |
140	|---|---|---|---|
141	| `FastList` | ✅ | `UICollectionView` with cell recycling | `RecyclerView` |
142	| `FastGrid` | ✅ | `UICollectionView` with cell recycling | `RecyclerView` |
143	| `MasonryFastGrid` | ✅ | Staggered Pinterest-style grid; heights from `itemHeightBuilder`. `UICollectionView` with a custom staggered layout | `RecyclerView` (`StaggeredGridLayoutManager`) |
144	
145	**Paging.** `FastList(pagingEnabled: true)` makes every swipe settle on exactly one item: a full-screen video feed, an onboarding carousel (`scrollDirection: Axis.horizontal`). The paging is the platform's own, so the feel is native and a fling moves one page. Each item is laid out at the list's own size, so a page is always one viewport. `PageView` is this with Flutter's names; use the `FastList` form when the feed also needs `keepAliveCount`, `onVisibleRange` or `stableItems`.
146	
147	**When to use `FastList` vs `ListView.builder`:**
148	
149	Both run on the platform's list (`UICollectionView` on iOS, `RecyclerView` on Android), which **recycles cell containers** so only on-screen cells are *drawn* and laid out — smooth scrolling at any length, even when rows change height as they load, and instant index-based jumps. Rows are built as they near the viewport, so the mount costs the same at any `itemCount`, and the rows more than 250 points off screen are let go, so content memory is bounded by that window, not by the rows the user has scrolled past. Keep Flutter code on `ListView.builder` as it is; reach for `FastList` for what only it has: `keepAliveCount` (the window in rows), `recycleItems`, paging, `onVisibleRange`, `onReorder`. Paginate when the data comes from a server — grow `itemCount` from the `onScroll` callback as the user nears the end — for the data's sake, not the list's.
150	
151	**Reusing rows.** Add `recycleItems: true` and the rows the window lets go are reused for the rows that scroll in, the way UIKit's lists and `RecyclerView` reuse their cells: a released row's widgets and native views are kept and updated with the next item's `itemBuilder` output instead of being torn down and built again. A row's native views are the expensive part of a list (a card is a few dozen of them), so a long fling then costs a few property updates per row. Keep the window small when rows are reused, a few rows on each side (`keepAliveCount: 4`): the rows outside it are what the list reuses, so a large window leaves a fling building fresh rows until it has gone past it. Rows must have the same shape for the reuse to be in place; an item of another widget type, or with another `key`, is built from scratch as usual. A reused row keeps its cell-local `State` across items, as a recycled cell does on the platform: a `StatefulWidget` in the row sees the new item in `didUpdateWidget` and resets what belonged to the old one there (an expanded state, a swipe offset), or keeps that state in the model.
152	
153	**The recipe for a long image list:**
154	
155	```dart
156	FastList(
157	  itemCount: photos.length,
158	  keepAliveCount: 4,                        // bound held content (the OOM killer)
159	  recycleItems: true,                       // reuse the rows the window lets go
160	  itemBuilder: (_, i) => Image.network(
161	    photos[i].url,
162	    cacheWidth: 300, cacheHeight: 300,      // bound each decoded bitmap
163	    fit: BoxFit.cover,
164	  ),
165	  onScroll: (offset, maxExtent, viewport, dragging) {
166	    if (maxExtent - offset < 2 * viewport) loadMore(); // bound itemCount
167	  },
168	)
169	```
170	
171	> ⚠️ Like Flutter's lazy lists beyond `cacheExtent`: a row outside the
172	> window loses any cell-local `State` (a checkbox, text being
173	> typed). Keep item state in your model, not in the cell. Tuning: placeholders
174	> on hard flings → raise `keepAliveCount`; memory too high → lower it or set
175	> `cacheWidth`/`cacheHeight`.
176	
177	### FastList properties
178	
179	FastList mirrors the `ListView.builder` API with the following configuration options:
180	
181	| Property | Type | Default | Description |
182	|---|---|---|---|
183	| `itemCount` | `int` | (required) | Total number of items in the list |
184	| `itemBuilder` | `Widget Function(BuildContext, int)` | (required) | Called for each visible index; returns a native widget |
185	| `scrollDirection` | `Axis` | `Axis.vertical` | Scroll axis; `horizontal` lays the children out in a row |
186	| `reverse` | `bool` | `false` | If `true`, list starts from the bottom |
187	| `showScrollBar` | `bool` | `false` | Show/hide the scroll indicator along the scroll axis |
188	| `padding` | `EdgeInsets?` | `null` | Content inset around the list |
189	| `physics` | `ScrollPhysics?` | `null` | `NeverScrollableScrollPhysics` to disable scrolling; `BouncingScrollPhysics` / `ClampingScrollPhysics` for scroll behaviour |
190	| `keepAliveCount` | `int?` | `null` | Content windowing in rows: keep built content only for visible rows + this many on each side (memory becomes independent of `itemCount`). `null` uses `cacheExtent` |
191	| `cacheExtent` | `double?` | `null` | The same window measured in points, as Flutter's `ListView.cacheExtent`: rows within that distance of the screen stay built, rows beyond it are let go; 250 points when neither this nor `keepAliveCount` is set, as in Flutter. Holds the same amount of content whatever a row holds (one card or a row of four). `keepAliveCount` wins when both are set |
192	| `recycleItems` | `bool` | `false` | Reuse the rows the window lets go for the rows that scroll in: their widgets and native views are updated to the new item instead of rebuilt. A reused row keeps its cell-local `State`, reset it in `didUpdateWidget` |
193	| `itemExtent` | `double?` | `null` | The main-axis size of every row when all rows are the same size, as Flutter's `ListView.itemExtent`: rows not built yet then take exactly that size, so the scroll bar and a jump to a far index are exact. Without it an unbuilt row takes the average of the rows measured so far |
194	| `onScroll` | `FastScrollCallback?` | `null` | Fires `(offset, maxExtent, viewport, dragging)` on scroll — load-more, hide-on-scroll, progress |
195	
196	> **Off-screen cells are reused by the native platform** (`UICollectionView` /
197	> `RecyclerView`), and the content of the rows around the screen is kept by
198	> `cacheExtent` (in points, as in Flutter) or `keepAliveCount` (in rows).
199	> Long-distance navigation is O(1): use
200	> [`FastListController.jumpToItem`](#fastlistcontroller) /
201	> `scrollToItem` / `animateToItem` to jump to **any** index instantly,
202	> regardless of how far it is off-screen. Their `alignment` rests the item
203	> at the top (`0.0`), the centre (`0.5`) or the bottom (`1.0`) of the list,
204	> on both platforms, animated or not; an animated scroll to an item far
205	> away is quick (on iOS the list moves the whole way in a third of a
206	> second, as the platform's own lists do, showing the rows of a few
207	> screens on the way; on Android it starts a screen short of the item),
208	> and it ends on the item even when rows near it change size as they are
209	> built. For scroll position (load-more,
210	> hide-on-scroll, progress), use the `onScroll(offset, maxExtent, viewport,
211	> dragging)` callback rather than a Flutter `ScrollController`.
212	> `ScrollController` works on every scrollable, horizontal ones included:
213	> `offset` and `position.pixels`/`maxScrollExtent` update live along the
214	> scroll axis, and `jumpTo`/`animateTo` drive the native scroll view along
215	> it. The dedicated Fast controllers add what a
216	> pixel offset cannot express — jumping to an item by index
217	> (`jumpToItem`) inside recycled content. Any of these controllers can be
218	> given or replaced by a rebuild: the new one drives the list from then on
219	> and the old one lets go. A controller moved to another list in the same
220	> rebuild stays with that list, as Flutter's `ScrollController` does.
221	
222	```dart
223	FastList(
224	  itemCount: items.length,
225	  itemBuilder: (context, index) => Text(items[index].title),
226	  showScrollBar: false,   // hide the scroll indicator
227	)
228	```

230	### FastGrid properties
231	
232	FastGrid is the grid counterpart, backed by `UICollectionView` (iOS) /
233	`RecyclerView` (Android). Same build-on-approach and recycle model as `FastList`,
234	with its own index-based `FastGridController` (`jumpToItem` / `scrollToItem`) and
235	the same `onScroll` callback. (`MasonryFastGrid` shares the `FastGridController`.)
236	
237	| Property | Type | Default | Description |
238	|---|---|---|---|
239	| `itemCount` | `int` | (required) | Total number of items |
240	| `itemBuilder` | `Widget Function(BuildContext, int)` | (required) | Called for each visible index |
241	| `crossAxisCount` | `int` | `2` | Number of columns |
242	| `maxCrossAxisExtent` | `double?` | `null` | The widest a cell may be: the grid takes as many columns as fit, from its width, as Flutter's `SliverGridDelegateWithMaxCrossAxisExtent`. Wins over `crossAxisCount` |
243	| `mainAxisSpacing` / `crossAxisSpacing` | `double` | `0.0` | Spacing between items |
244	| `padding` | `EdgeInsets?` | `null` | Content inset |
245	| `cacheExtent` | `double?` | `null` | How far beyond the screen, in points, cells stay built: 250 when neither this nor `keepAliveCount` is set, as in Flutter |
246	| `keepAliveCount` | `int?` | `null` | The same window counted in cells on each side; wins over `cacheExtent` |
247	
248	Like `FastList`, the native view recycles cell containers for smooth scrolling,
249	cells are built as they near the viewport (a cell's size comes from the grid's
250	own configuration, so an unbuilt cell needs nothing and `itemCount` is not a
251	cost), and both grids keep built content only for a window around the screen,
252	250 points on each side by default: content memory is O(visible + the window),
253	independent of `itemCount`. `keepAliveCount` counts **items, not rows** —
254	multiply by your column count (a 3-column grid wants ~3× a list's value).
255	Combine with `Image.cacheWidth`/`cacheHeight` for the full recipe. A cell's
256	content fills the cell, as in Flutter.
257	
258	```dart
259	FastGrid(
260	  itemCount: photos.length,
261	  itemBuilder: (context, index) => Image.network(photos[index].url),
262	  crossAxisCount: 3,
263	  mainAxisSpacing: 2,
264	  crossAxisSpacing: 2,
265	)
266	```
